claims.text: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) operates a national supermarket chain with a focus on value-retailing, offering a wide range of products in Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG), and General Merchandise & Apparel categories.

cites.quote: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.

claims.text: DMart operates 500 stores across 15 states, 1 Union Territory, and NCR, with a retail business area of 20.58 million sq. ft.

cites.quote: DMart has grown steadily over the years, and operates 500 stores in 15 States, 1 Union Territory and NCR.

claims.text: DMart's strategy is based on the Everyday Low Cost/Everyday Low Price (EDLC/EDLP) principle, aiming to offer good quality products at great value.

cites.quote: We remain focussed on our strategy of offering our customers good quality products at great value, based on the Everyday Low Cost/Everyday Low Price (EDLC/EDLP) principle.

claims.text: DMart's revenue for Q2 FY27 was 19,644 crore, reflecting a year-over-year growth of 17.8%.
The company's PAT for Q2 FY27 was 743 crore, showing a year-over-year increase of 8.5%.
For FY26, DMart reported a revenue of 68,821 crore and a PAT margin of 4.3%.
DMart's EBITDA margin for FY26 was 7.6%.
DMart's revenue grew at a CAGR of 15.9% from FY25 to FY26, increasing from 59,358 crore to 68,821 crore.
The company's PAT grew at a CAGR of 9.7% from FY25 to FY26.
DMart added 85 new stores in FY26, increasing its total to 500 stores.
DMart's total borrowings for FY26 were 965 crore, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x.
The company's net worth stood at 24,462 crore as of FY26.
DMart's CFO to PAT ratio improved from 91% in FY25 to 117% in FY26, indicating better cash conversion.
The company reported negative free cash flow of -647 crore in FY26, an improvement from -960 crore in FY25.
DMart's revenue growth of 15.9% in FY26 aligns with the management's focus on expanding store count and retail area.

cites.quote: Over the years we have seen steady growth in the number of stores and consequently our retail business area.

claims.text: The EBITDA margin of 7.6% in FY26 falls short of the 14%-15% target set for FY25, indicating a divergence from management's expectations.

cites.quote: We are targeting an EBITDA margin of around 14%-15%.

claims.text: Management's guidance on store openings has been aggressive, yet the actual number of stores opened in FY26 was 85, which is below the 60-store target for FY26.

cites.quote: We are ready to even open 60 stores.
